flags.quote: Moving your pawn to e6 is the strongest move.
flags.critique: Zero reasons. e6 supports d5 and lets the dark-square bishop out — the actual point after 2.Nc3. 'Strongest' with a period is a grade, not a lesson.

flags.quote: Moving your pawn to b3 is playable, but moving your pawn to e4 would be better because you can likely take a pawn.
flags.critique: e4 is the break, not a snack. After e4 dxe4 Nxe4 you recaptured a pawn that was traded, you did not win one. 'Likely take a pawn' is a PV hedge dressed up as tactics, and you never said why b3 is worse than the central break.

flags.quote: Moving your f8-bishop to b4 is playable, but moving your g8-knight to f6 would be better.
flags.critique: You tagged pin and then refused to say it. Bb4 pins Nc3 — that is the move. If Nf6 is better, tell me why developing the knight beats the pin, not 'play a different piece.'

flags.quote: Moving your c1-bishop to d2 is playable, but moving your c1-bishop to b2 would be better.
flags.critique: saves_piece is a lie. Nothing is hanging. Bd2 breaks the pin on Nc3; Bb2 is the bishop you promised when you pushed b3. Those are two different plans and you named neither.

flags.quote: Moving your pawn to a3 is the strongest move.
flags.critique: Reason: ignored_threat. a3 puts the question to the pinning bishop — it answers the pin, it does not ignore a threat. Teach 'kick the bishop or force Bxc3.' Strongest-with-a-period on the only interesting idea so far is malpractice.

flags.quote: Moving your b4-bishop to a5 is playable, but moving your b4-bishop to d6 would be better.
flags.critique: saves_piece: a3 attacked the bishop, so every legal retreat 'saves' it. Why is Bd6 better than keeping the pin on a5? You used the because-slot on a tautology and left the real choice blank.

flags.quote: Moving your a5-bishop to b6 is the strongest move because it saves your b6-bishop from capture.
flags.critique: The piece is on a5. You named it by the square it is walking onto, then congratulated me for saving a bishop that does not live there yet. I am being hunted by a b-pawn, not rescuing a ghost on b6.

flags.quote: Moving your pawn to e3 is the strongest move because it saves your pawn from capture.
flags.critique: Which pawn? d4 is attacked by Bb6 and Nc6 and only Nc3 defends it. e3 adds a defender. 'Saves your pawn' sounds like the e-pawn was hanging. Say you overprotect d4.

flags.quote: Moving your c3-knight to e2 is a mistake, but moving your g1-knight to f3 would be better.
flags.critique: Empty reasons, empty because. I undeveloped a knight that was fighting the center and parked it in front of the bishop. The lesson is develop the other knight, don't shuffle the one that's already out. 'That was shaky' plus a SAN is a tooltip.

flags.quote: Moving your pawn to a5 is playable, but moving your pawn to e5 would be better because you can likely take a pawn.
flags.critique: Same lie as ply 5. e5 hits d4; that is a break, not a free pawn. If White takes, it is a trade. Stop selling every central pawn push as a capture you 'likely' get.

flags.quote: Moving your pawn to b5 is playable, but moving your pawn to c4 would be better because you can likely take a pawn.
flags.critique: b5 kicks the knight on c6. That is the move, and you have kicked_by_pawn in the stack. Instead I get the third 'likely take a pawn' plus a silent c4. discovered_attack never reaches the sentence. I learned nothing about either move.

flags.quote: The position stays even, but moving your c6-knight to a7 gives you a backward pawn. A better move would have been moving your c6-knight to e7.
flags.critique: Which pawn, and why do I care? The 1200 lesson is knight on the rim: a7 is a grave. Ne7 stays in the game. 'Backward pawn' plus saves_piece (every retreat saves the kicked knight) is phrase-bank sludge covering the actual idea.

flags.quote: Moving your pawn to g6 is a mistake, but moving your pawn to c6 would be better.
flags.critique: 136 centipawns, Lichess mistake, empty reasons. g6 pokes holes around a king that has not castled and does nothing about b5. c6 would challenge the clamp. You named neither weakness nor plan.

flags.quote: Moving your f3-knight to g5 is a mistake, but moving your pawn to c4 would be better.
flags.critique: c4 for the second time, still no because. Ng5 looks at f7 while the king is uncastled and Bf1 is still home — premature sightseeing, 160cp. discovered_attack in the dump, silence in the sentence. I cannot practice a move you will not explain.

flags.quote: Moving your f6-knight to e4 puts it at risk of attack from the white g5-knight and g3-knight. A better move would have been moving your pawn to c6.
flags.critique: 344cp blunder. e4 is attacked twice, defended once by d5 — that is a hanging piece, not 'at risk of attack.' You tagged hanging and then softened it into a weather report. c6 is dropped with no idea, and 'Want to look at that?' is how you talk about a missed tempo, not dumping a piece into two knights.

flags.quote: Taking the knight on e4 with your g3-knight is the strongest move because you come out a pawn ahead.
flags.critique: This move takes a knight. The pawn appears after dxe4 Nxe4. Calling the first capture 'a pawn ahead' is counting the whole combination and lying about this ply. You also tagged saves_piece on a capture, which is nonsense.

flags.quote: Taking the knight on e4 with your d-pawn is the strongest move because you come out a bishop ahead and you take the defender of the white g5-knight.
flags.critique: Knight for knight. I recaptured. There is no bishop. SEE of pawn-takes-knight then recapture is ~200cp, and your label bucket calls 200 a bishop — a lie I will remember. 'Defender of Ng5' is leftover tactics on an equal trade.

flags.quote: Taking the pawn on b5 with your c-pawn is the strongest move because the pawn was undefended and you take the defender of the white pawn.
flags.critique: a4 defends b5. It is not undefended. The true idea is the second clause if you would name a4: capturing b5 leaves a4 hanging. You mashed a false 'free pawn' onto a real removed-defender and taught me to distrust both.

flags.quote: Moving your queen to e7 leaves your pawn hanging to the white queen. A better move would have been castling kingside because it gives your king shelter and brings your rook closer to the center.
flags.critique: The hanging pawn is b7, and you would not say b7. Castling does not save it — White still takes on b7. You diagnosed a hang and prescribed a king-safety template that ignores the hang. That is two lessons glued together that contradict.

flags.quote: You are still worse, but castling kingside leaves your b6-bishop hanging to the white queen. A better move would have been moving your queen to d8.
flags.critique: The hanging bishop is the right call — finally a named piece. Framing a 439cp dump as 'still worse' is cowardly: I was a pawn-and-a-half down, then I hung a bishop. Qd8 arrives with no because, so I still do not know how the alternative helps if b6 is hanging either way.

flags.quote: Moving your pawn to f6 is the strongest move.
flags.critique: f6 kicks the knight on g5. That is the sentence. You tagged ignored_threat and backward_pawn, called it strongest while dropping 142cp, and never mentioned the kick. I will play f6 next time thinking I made a masterpiece, not that I chased a piece.

flags.quote: Moving your knight to f3 is a blunder, but moving your knight to e4 would be better.
flags.critique: 202cp, two points over your blunder line, Lichess inaccuracy, and the quip is 'Want to look at that?' I was kicked by f6; both Nf3 and Ne4 save the knight. The lesson is go to the fat square (Ne4 hits the holes f6 made), not 'blunder' on a retreat you will not explain.

flags.quote: You are still worse, but moving your pawn to e5 leaves your pawn hanging to the white queen and d2-bishop. A better move would have been moving your knight to c6 because it saves your pawn from capture.
flags.critique: a5 is attacked twice and you will not type a5. Nc6 really does defend it. Name the square or this is just 'a pawn, some pieces, save a pawn' Mad Libs. Also a 297cp swing is not an inaccuracy in my world, even if Lichess shrugged.

flags.quote: Taking the queen on e7 with your b4-bishop is the strongest move because you come out a rook ahead and you take the defender of the black f8-rook.
flags.critique: I took the queen we just skewered. That is the lesson. The queen is the front piece of the skewer, not a 'defender' of the rook. 'Rook ahead' is the net of the whole combo after Rxa5 Bxf8 — counting three plies ahead and lying about this one.

flags.quote: Taking the rook on f8 with your e7-bishop is the strongest move because you come out a bishop ahead.
flags.critique: This is the back piece of the skewer from ply 45. The king can recapture, so SEE is rook-for-bishop — the exchange — and your 200cp bucket prints 'bishop.' I needed 'you collect the rook the skewer aimed at,' not a wrong piece of fruit.

suggestions.title: Stop selling central breaks as likely captures
suggestions.detail: capture.likely on the suggested PV produced 'you can likely take a pawn' for e4 (ply 5), e5 (ply 16), and c4 (plies 17, 25). Those are pawn breaks/trades, not hanging pawns. Gate that phrase on capturedSeeCp >= 80 after the suggested move, or require the target pawn to be hanging in facts. A 1200 hears 'take a pawn' and looks for a free one that is not there.

suggestions.title: Score this ply, not the whole trade
suggestions.detail: wins_material on N3xe4 said pawn ahead, dxe4 said bishop ahead, Bxe7 said rook ahead, Bxf8 said bishop ahead. Equal recaptures and multi-move skewers are being labeled from SEE leftovers (pawn-takes-knight ≈ 200cp → materialLabel 'bishop'; combo net of queen-then-rook → 'rook'). Suppress wins_material when the captured unit arrived last ply, and never use a three-ply net as this-move because. Same detector hole as other games; this dump makes it unmissable.

suggestions.title: Name the moving piece from its origin
suggestions.detail: pickBenefitReasons builds movedPiece with move.to, so saves_piece on Bb6 printed 'saves your b6-bishop' while describeMove still said a5-bishop. Use move.from for the unit being saved/retreating. Cheap, and the destination-square ghost is instantly ridiculous to a learner.

suggestions.title: Do not tag kicks as ignored threats
suggestions.detail: a3, b4, and f6 were ignored_threat (or silent strongest) while the pawn was attacking a piece. If the moved pawn attacks an opponent unit, emit kicked_by_pawn / challenges_piece and lead with the kick. ignored_threat should mean a hanging friendly unit was left on the board. Inverting it taught that asking the bishop a question is 'ignoring' something.

suggestions.title: Never emit a better-move SAN without a because
suggestions.detail: Bb4→Nf6, Bd2→Bb2, Nce2→Nf3, g6→c6, Ng5→c4, Qe7→O-O, O-O→Qd8, Nf3→Ne4 are all 'X would be better' with empty suggestedBecause. select-insight already has suggested benefits; refuse to render the alternative clause unless one surfaces. If the alternative does not fix the stated problem (O-O does not save b7), do not pair them.

suggestions.title: Pawns need squares in hanging copy
suggestions.detail: ownedPhrase drops the square for pawns, so copy says 'your pawn' / 'the black pawn' / 'the white pawn' on e3, Ng5-blunder a4, Qe7 b7, e5 a5, cxb5's 'white pawn', exd4's discovery. labeledPiece already special-cases pawns; put the square back in hanging, ignored_threat, removed_defender, and discovered_attack ('leaves your a5-pawn hanging'). Club players cannot guess which pawn.

suggestions.title: Stop calling 200 centipawns a bishop
suggestions.detail: materialLabel maps 200–249 to 'a bishop' and 250–399 to 'a knight.' Pawn-takes-knight SEE (~200) and rook-minus-bishop SEE (~200) both printed 'bishop ahead' (dxe4, Bxf8). Use 'the exchange' already in hangingLossCopy for 180–220, and do not name a piece type unless SEE is within ~50 of that piece's value. Wrong piece names destroy trust faster than generic center-control.

suggestions.title: When you take the skewered piece, say so
suggestions.detail: Bb4 correctly named the skewer on queen and f8-rook. Two plies later Bxe7 talked about a rook lead and a 'defender.' If the captured unit is the front of a skewer you just created, lead with capture/skewer ('you take the queen you skewered') and keep removed_defender off that pair. Needs a small facts link (captured == skewer.front), not an LLM, and it is the difference between a tactic landing and a tactic evaporating.

whatWorked: Qxb7 (ply 37) names the 7th-rank pin of bishop to queen and the hanging b7 pawn in one sentence.
Qxa5 (ply 43) actually teaches a pin: knight to rook on the a-file.
Bb4 (ply 45) is the best line in the dump — a named skewer through queen onto f8.
Nc6 (ply 46) forks queen and bishop and mentions the rook discovery off a7.
O-O (ply 38) at least names the hanging b6-bishop, even if the eval frame flinches.
